title: Location Tracking via GPS Data in Transit
description: GPS position data transmitted in the data flow can be intercepted and used to track the user's movements over time, potentially revealing sensitive patterns of life, home/work locations, and daily routines.

title: User Identification from Sensor Telemetry
description: The combination of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps in transit can be analyzed to uniquely identify the user, especially when correlated with other data sources.

title: User Unawareness of Data Collection Scope
description: The user may not fully understand what sensor data is being continuously captured, how it's being used, or who has access to it, leading to uninformed consent.

title: Insecure Data Storage at Wearable Device
description: The wearable device may store sensitive health and location data without adequate encryption or access controls, exposing it to unauthorized access if the device is lost, stolen, or compromised.

title: Linkability of location data during transmission
description: GPS traces transmitted between wearable and app could be linked to identify the user's movements and patterns, potentially enabling tracking across different contexts or sessions.

title: Unauthorized data disclosure at destination
description: The companion app could store or share sensitive sensor data (GPS traces, device ID) with unauthorized parties or for purposes beyond user consent, leading to privacy violations.

title: Identification through device data sharing
description: The wearable device shares device ID and location data that could be used to identify the user, especially if the device is compromised or data is intercepted during transmission.

title: Excessive data collection during transmission
description: The device transmits more data (GPS traces, device ID, timestamps) than may be necessary for the stated purpose of syncing exercise sessions, potentially violating data minimization principles.

title: Identification of User through Health Data
description: Manual logging of calorie intake, meals, and weight entries could be used to identify the user, especially if combined with other data sources or metadata.

title: Linkability of User Data
description: The manually entered health data could be linked to the user's identity or other data sources, potentially revealing patterns about the user's lifestyle, health conditions, or behaviors.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Health Data
description: The companion mobile app could store or process the health data in a way that exposes it to unauthorized parties, either through security vulnerabilities or improper access controls.

title: Unintended Use of Health Data
description: The health data collected could be used for purposes beyond the user's original intent, such as for advertising, insurance underwriting, or third-party data sharing without explicit consent.

title: Data Manipulation in Transit
description: The manually entered health data could be altered or tampered with during transmission between the user and the companion mobile app, compromising data integrity.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Health log data (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) transmitted from the mobile app to the health log store could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if not properly encrypted during transit.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Health Data
description: Once stored in the health log store, sensitive health information could be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems without proper access controls, leading to privacy violations.

title: Direct Identification Through Health Logs
description: Health logs contain personal health information that could directly identify individuals, potentially revealing sensitive medical conditions, behaviors, or lifestyle patterns.

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Health Log Entries
description: Users may not be able to prove who created or modified specific health log entries, as the system may not maintain adequate audit trails or cryptographic signatures.

title: Denial of Service to Health Log Store
description: The health log store could be overwhelmed by excessive data writes or malicious requests, preventing legitimate users from accessing or updating their health data.

title: Identification through Location Data Collection
description: The mobile app collects and shares precise GPS location traces with timestamps, which can be used to identify individuals based on their movement patterns, routines, and frequent locations.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: The location history store may be accessible to unauthorized parties, allowing them to view or extract sensitive location data without proper authentication or authorization.

title: Data Misuse Beyond Original Purpose
description: The location history store may use the collected location data for purposes beyond the original intent (e.g., profiling, advertising, or sharing with third parties) without user consent.

title: Loss of Anonymity through Location Tracing
description: The act of sharing location data with timestamps can reveal sensitive personal information about the user's habits, associations, and daily routines, compromising their anonymity.

title: Unauthorized Access to Health Analytics Data
description: The Health Analytics Service may store or process health log data in ways that allow unauthorized parties to access sensitive health information, including calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions.

title: Re-identification from Aggregated Health Data
description: Health-condition analysis across multiple sessions may produce patterns or aggregated data that could be used to re-identify individuals, especially when combined with other data sources.

title: Linkability of Health Data Across Sessions
description: The analytics service may link health data across different sessions, creating a comprehensive health profile that could be used to infer sensitive information about the user's health conditions and behaviors.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Health log data in transit between the Health Log Store and Analytics Service could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, exposing sensitive personal health information.

title: User Unawareness of Cross-Session Analysis
description: Users may not be aware that their health logs are being analyzed across multiple sessions, leading to lack of informed consent for the extent of data processing.

title: Linkability of Location Data in Transit
description: Location history data transferred between datastore and analytics service could be intercepted or monitored, enabling linkage of movement patterns across sessions to identify individuals or correlate with other data sources.

title: Identification via Location Patterns
description: Location data in transit contains movement patterns that could be used to identify specific individuals based on their daily routines and habitual locations.

title: Identification of Individuals from Routine Analysis
description: The health analytics service processes location history to derive daily routines and movement patterns, which could uniquely identify individuals even when direct identifiers are removed.

title: Unawareness of Location Pattern Analysis
description: Users may not be aware that their location history is being analyzed across sessions to derive daily routines and movement patterns, violating informed consent principles.

title: Disclosure of Movement Patterns
description: Derived movement patterns and daily routines could be disclosed to unauthorized parties or used for purposes beyond the original intent, such as insurance underwriting or employer monitoring.

title: Linkability at Source of Location History
description: The act of sharing location history from the datastore enables linkage of data across multiple sessions, potentially revealing comprehensive movement profiles of individuals.

title: Identifiability of Health Insights
description: The Health Analytics Service shares inferred health insights (risk indicators, routine summaries, trend flags) that could potentially identify the user when combined with other data sources or metadata.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Health Data
description: The source element shares sensitive health-condition risk indicators and personal health summaries without adequate access controls, creating risk of unauthorized disclosure to unintended recipients.

title: Linkability of Health Data Across Services
description: Health insights transmitted in this flow could be linked with other data sources (e.g., device identifiers, usage patterns) to create a comprehensive profile of the user across multiple services.

title: Inadequate Protection of Received Health Data
description: The Companion Mobile App may not adequately protect the received health insights, potentially exposing sensitive health information through insecure storage or transmission to third parties.

title: Unauthorized Access to Health Analytics
description: The destination element may lack proper access controls, allowing unauthorized users or processes to access the health insights received from the analytics service.

title: Sensitive Health Information Disclosure
description: The mobile app displays sensitive health risk indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) to the user, potentially exposing private medical information that could be intercepted or observed by unauthorized parties.

title: Health Data Inference by Third Parties
description: The displayed health trend indicators could allow third parties to infer the user's medical condition or health status through observation of the app dashboard, even if the raw data is not directly shared.

title: Psychological Harm from Health Risk Display
description: Displaying eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals to the user may cause unintended psychological distress, anxiety, or negative behavioral responses, particularly if the user is vulnerable or misinterprets the risk indicators.

title: User Identification Through Health Data
description: The combination of displayed health risk indicators and user-specific data could enable identification of the user to others, especially if the health signals are unique or rare.

title: Unauthorized Access to Health Dashboard
description: The user's health dashboard may be accessible to unauthorized individuals (family members, friends, or malicious actors) who could view sensitive health information without proper authentication or consent.

title: Data Interception During Transit
description: Health and location data transmitted to cloud provider could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially revealing personally identifiable information about individuals.

title: Metadata Exposure in Transit
description: Metadata accompanying the data flow (e.g., timestamps, data sizes, access patterns) could be used to infer information about the parties involved or the nature of the data being shared.

title: Unauthorized Access at Cloud Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider may have inadequate security controls, allowing unauthorized access to the hosted health and location datasets, potentially leading to data breaches.

title: Data Sharing with Third Parties
description: The cloud provider may share or sell the hosted health and location data to third parties without proper authorization or consent from data subjects.

title: Data Degradation Through Improper Storage
description: The cloud provider may store the health and location data inappropriately (e.g., insufficient encryption, inadequate access controls), leading to data degradation or loss of privacy protections.

title: Inappropriate Data Sharing by Source
description: The health analytics service may share full health and location datasets without proper consent or legal basis, exposing individuals to privacy risks from the act of sharing itself.
